Coinbase insiders dumped hundreds of millions of dollars worth of $COIN. Much of this near the top, over $250 per share.

The co-founder of Coinbase, who is also founder of Paradigm, was a big part of that selling. He also bought the recent sell off, near the all time low.

Smart trade, right? I’m not throwing shade on him. This is how it’s always done. I mention him only because of the obvious relationship to Coinbase.

Now out of the blue about 5 days ago, Coinbase announced to much fanfare that “the first viral social dapp on Base” just launched.

This drove a massive amount of traffic to its new Base protocol. Well of course it did. It’s an influencer pumped ponzi. They take off fast and they’re exponentially sticky.

But why Friendtech?

2 days later we found out, as Paradigm announced its involvement as backers of the app. Activity exploded as that seemed to suggest that the platform is legit. Not a phishing scheme as many suspected early on.

So what’s the problem?

Friendtech has launched under the guise of being a token gated private chat for influencers. The platform is incredibly buggy. But that didn’t matter. The idea is intriguing, howeber the mechanics are set up to destroy retail.

So far we’ve seen influencers profit tremendously by buying their own shares (which are tokens) and burning them into the bonding curve. This manipulation of individual share prices has already made large sums of money for influencers. Some are over six figures in a few days of doing essentially nothing.

The Friendtech platform itself is raking in millions of dollars, as it takes a 10% fee (same as the influencer) on every transaction on the steep bonding curve. Share prices scale fast. We’ve seen this before and it never ends well.

Coinbase got a ton of network activity, which ultimately it will use as proof of concept when selling stock to retail investors that probably are not aware it’s just a ponzi.

Paradigm, which is connected to Coinbase through its founder and others, is raking in the cash now likely in the millions of dollars through platform fees.

Influencers are dreaming up wild and creative ways to manipulate their share prices on the platform. Some will certainly make hundreds of thousands or even millions of dollars off this.

Retail will undoubtedly get rekt in this high stakes game of musical chairs. It’s inevitable that retail will be left holding the bag as the shares on the bonding curve fall in price just as fast as they rise once the hype is gone and the music stops.

Coinbase will likely rope in new retail investors excited to own a piece of Base, not realizing that the utility is tied to an unsustainable ponzi. The money can’t magically appear out of nowhere, so there has to be a loser here.

Some retail traders of Friendtech shares have done well. You can make money in a ponzi if you’re early. Look at Terra or even Madoff. Some massive early retail winners that got out on time. But it’s a stacked deck.

In this case retail is even further disadvantaged because they’re getting front run by bots. And the shameless sellers of these bots are front running their own bot buying customers. The rabbit hole runs deep.

Everybody wins, and retail loses.

Again, this isn’t a criticism of Coinbase, its insiders or Paradigm, or its partners. This is how things are done and there’s nothing new here to see. But it’s a heads up to retail. 

Excercise extreme caution here. This time is not different. It will not end well, and just know that you’re the exit liquidity.

Ethereum validators could get paid to protect trades.

@ETHGasOfficial is building a market where institutions can pay participating validators for committed inclusion in upcoming blocks. Their trades go directly to ETHGas and never sit in the public mempool where pending transactions are visible to everyone.

Specialized traders called searchers watch the mempool for large trades and pay to place their own orders right before and after them. They profit from the price move and the original trader can get a worse fill.

Going through ETHGas limits that exposure, and under this model, an institution buying a whole block could set the order of transactions inside it.

What institutions pay for this could become a new revenue stream for validators. Regulated buyers want to know who is handling their trades and could choose to use only identity-verified validators. 

Each trade would then wait for one of them to propose a block. The average wait is about two minutes if that group runs 10% of Ethereum's stake and about 24 seconds at 50%.

Adding more verified stake shortens the wait for the institutions paying them.

On Sunday, OpenAI's chief scientist called the thing his company builds "an alien mind" and asked rival labs to agree on a speed limit for it. A few hours later, Meta's chief AI officer used nearly the same words about the Claude-assisted Riemann proof, "completed with the help of an alien mind that we don't understand," and declared that superintelligence is arriving.

In between, Elon Musk posted to 53,000 likes: "Consciousness is either an illusion or ubiquitous on a gradient. Difficult to argue that carbon is conscious, but silicon is not." Meanwhile, the proof that set off the weekend has been certified by software, is roughly 250,000 pages long by one estimate, and the Clay Institute still lists the problem as unsolved.

So by Sunday night the industry agreed the machine is alien, possibly conscious, better at math than anyone alive, and in need of a cap.

Philosophers spent 2,500 years asking what a mind is. OpenAI answered with a number, then asked everyone to promise not to make it any smaller.

BEFORE IT WAS OBVIOUS: @coinbase. You can be wrong about the market and right about the founder.

@TimDraper almost missed Coinbase.

In his account, @brian_armstrong originally pitched Coinbase to Joel Yarmon and Tim. Draper liked Armstrong, but the firm had already invested in CoinLab, a Bitcoin exchange focused on institutional investors. They made a strategic judgment: Coinbase was going after retail consumers, and they thought that route would take too long. So Draper passed.

His son @AdamDraper saw it differently. Adam Draper met Brian separately and wrote Coinbase his first check. Then the market started answering the question.

Coinbase grew, consumer adoption accelerated. Crypto moved far beyond the relatively small audience that existed when the company was founded. And when Coinbase raised another round, Draper Associates invested. Tim writes that the Coinbase investment ultimately returned nearly twice the size of an entire Draper Associates fund.

There’s an important lesson buried in the part of the story where they were initially wrong. The team correctly recognized Brian Armstrong as exceptional, but underestimated the path he had chosen.

Why it matters for builders: investors can be wrong about your market timing, your customer, or even your entire strategy while still recognizing something unusual in you. And investors should remember the inverse: sometimes the unconventional go-to-market strategy is exactly what creates the enormous market.

Retail crypto looked like the longer road, yet it became the road to mass adoption.

We believe the best measure of intelligence is the ability to predict the future. Doing so requires learning about the past and constantly working to be less wrong.

The ETH papers were also released in an similar oneupmanship fashion. As with Anthropic's result, no name on the paper (my guess is this was GPT-Aeon). Also like Anthropic: no announcement, no blog post, no tweet. 

This is a significant result, yet both OpenAI and Anthropic chose to simply dump it online with no comment. I was listening to a Scott Aaronson interview this morning where he said this specific result would update him toward 'a solution to P ≠ NP by the AIs might really be around the corner.'
To me this is more evidence for my argument that both OpenAI and Anthropic are sitting on a dragon's hoard of scientific results they are not releasing to the public. The first massive 700+ paper OpenAI GitHub dump took five weeks for their model to generate. It's been seven weeks since then, and their internal model has continued to improve. They said they had it working on 4,000 problems. How many have been solved in the last seven weeks? Based on the last release, 1,000+ is not unreasonable.

I will quote OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki from the blog post 'Perplexity and Intelligence,' posted 48 hours ago:

'We have recently witnessed unprecedented acceleration in another domain. For more than a year, we have been posing open problems in mathematics to our models as one of the ways of evaluating them. Once we upgraded to a model of log-perplexity ~0.76, it started producing groundbreaking results. For many of us that have previously worked in mathematics and adjacent fields, seeing the resolutions to questions we've long thought about coming out of the model one after another in a single Slack thread felt deeply surreal.'

There have also been, of late, multiple rumors about breakthroughs in cryptography that I have been reluctant to post about for obvious reasons. Specifically, there have been rumors of an encryption breakthrough at Anthropic. What I personally took from the big OpenAI math release was that all encryption will be cracked much sooner than people are expecting, and that the rate of scientific discoveries will continually increase as we continue to scale up. No, not will increase, *has increased*. At both labs. We just don't know about it yet. Because unless you work at those labs, the current frontier is completely invisible. But it won't stay that way forever. Or to put it another way: prepare yourself for revelations.

@NaveenGRao sold Nervana to Intel and MosaicML to Databricks. His third company, @unconvai, is building something that looks nothing like a GPU.

The scheme looks more and more likely to be enshrined in Bitcoin's consensus code every day that goes by—with a full security analysis published by the team just last week. 

More importantly, there is shockingly little contention around this scheme (outside of an appropriate level of tradeoff/risk assessment) since the scheme specification was published in September.

For additional clarity on developers' posture around quantum—I'm not exaggerating when I say *the majority* of the most prominent Bitcoin developers in the world are now working on quantum, with many funded full time or, at a minimum, regularly engaged in serious review on the mailing list and other forums. 

Many of these developers have completely halted other projects to focus exclusively on Quantum... or AI-relevant security, which thank God is also getting the attention it deserves right now. 

This all to say, the developers seem more than capable of "making a decision" on this one—this take is about as stale as sour milk.
